correctness.rationale: For the 9+9 bipartite incidence graph, a maximal matching leaves independent uncovered sets of equal sizes. Four chosen points meet at least six of nine selected lines, excluding cardinality below six. Exactly eighteen affine triangles leave three avoiding lines, and on each twelve-vertex complement three forced edges plus one six-cycle give exactly two perfect matchings. Exhaustive first-free-vertex recursion gives cardinality counts (36,567,648,42), and an independent LCF model verifies no four-by-four cocliques and all 36 minima. Both scripts exhaustively check 630 optimum pairs, the 126 three-swap edges, 36 BFS profiles (1,7,12,12,4), and finite affine symmetry transitivity. Finite enumeration is exhaustive and no infinite-generalization inference is made.

A Pappus secure-domination census has 1,755 optimum eight-vertex guards and a different token-relocation metric; a Pappus local perfect-matching forcing result concerns 42 perfect matchings and forcing triples, not 36 nonperfect maximal matchings.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither graph transfer nor predicate inclusion can identify the 36 maximal six-edge Pappus matchings with 27 maximum induced matchings or 42 perfect matchings. The prior Heawood Coxeter graph identification is not a universal theorem for cubic incidence graphs and does not imply these Pappus parameters. The new sharp three-edge threshold and 7-regular radius-four graph are logically additional. The existing Pappus skew-zero-forcing, secure-domination and perfect-matching forcing statements are about vertex placements or certificates for perfect matchings and do not imply a classification or the mobility of minimum maximal matchings.

value.rationale: This natural highly symmetric incidence graph has 36 optimal independent edge-dominating placements characterized by 18 affine geometry cores, with precisely two matchings per core. One- and two-edge moves freeze every optimum, while three-edge moves connect all optima in a vertex-transitive seven-regular graph with sharp four-step diameter, distinguishing optimal sensor count from practical relocation flexibility. The exact geometric and exchange structure is not merely another numerical minimum or arbitrary slice; it is motivated by edge domination and optimal reconfiguration.
